title: The Second Letter of Peter
lead: A short letter written as the apostle Peter's farewell: grow in the virtues that make your calling firm, remember the apostles and prophets, beware of false teachers, and keep waiting for the day of the Lord. It is the most doubted book of the New Testament, and its chapter 2 reworks the letter of Jude.

sections.b: The letter claims to be by "Simeon Peter" (2 Peter 1:1), an eyewitness of the transfiguration (2 Peter 1:16–18), writing near his death (2 Peter 1:14). Most critical scholars think a follower wrote it in his name, probably late in the first century: it uses Jude, its Greek differs from 1 Peter's, and it speaks of "the fathers" as dead and of Paul's letters as a collection. A minority defend Peter's authorship, perhaps with a secretary. The early church was slow to accept it, but by the late 300s it was received everywhere.
